title: Hierarchical Reduction of Invariant Subspaces: From Fragmentation to Many-Body Scars
abstract: We investigate a hierarchy of invariant Hilbert-space structures connecting Hilbert-space fragmentation, partial solvability, and quantum many-body scars. For spin chains with fragmented spin-$1/2$ subspaces and their local deformations, we show, using the spin-$1$ $XXC$ chain as a representative example, how successive local deformations reduce extensive irreducible-string fragmentation through an implicitly embedded spin-$1/2$ invariant space and ultimately to a single scar tower, connecting the $XXC$, perturbed $XXC$, and spin-$1$ $XY$ scar models. Through the intermediate embedded space, local dynamics couples states from distinct frozen irreducible-string sectors and selects a new decomposition into representations, from which smaller invariant spaces can be retained. We also establish a rigidity constraint on isolating nonsymmetric towers and a constructive correspondence that transfers a reduction between locally realizable representations of the embedded dynamics. The latter demonstrates that the reduction hierarchy can be transferred through a unitary transformation within the embedded subspace, yielding an exact scar tower built on a Néel reference state without requiring unitary equivalence of the full Hamiltonians.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to understand how complex quantum systems, initially exhibiting fragmented Hilbert spaces, undergo a systematic reduction in complexity. By analyzing the role of embedded invariant subspaces, the authors show that these systems can be reduced to simple, robust structures known as quantum many-body scars. This provides a powerful algebraic tool for analyzing dynamics in strongly correlated quantum materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates the hierarchical reduction of invariant Hilbert-space structures, tracing a path from initial Hilbert-space fragmentation to partial solvability and finally to quantum many-body scars.
main_result: Local deformations can systematically reduce extensive irreducible-string fragmentation through an embedded invariant subspace to a single, robust scar tower, even without requiring the full Hamiltonians to be unitarily equivalent.
method: The analysis employs representation theory and constructive correspondence to map the reduction hierarchy through unitary transformations within intermediate, embedded subspaces.
model_or_system: The study focuses on spin chains, using the spin-1 XXC chain as a primary example, which exhibits Hilbert-space fragmentation due to local interactions.
key_observables: Irreducible-string fragmentation sectors, the embedded spin-1/2 invariant subspace ($W_{	ext{emb}}$), and the resulting scar tower structure.
important_parameters: The nature of local deformations, the relationship between interaction range ($r$) and block period ($p$), and the symmetry constraints ($	ext{U}(1)$ conservation).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of specific invariant subspaces and the ability to transfer reduction structures via unitary transformations within these embedded spaces.

why_interesting: The systematic mapping of complex, fragmented dynamics onto simpler, structured invariant subspaces (like scar towers) provides powerful theoretical tools for analyzing quasi-integrable quantum systems relevant to AMO and condensed matter physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic hierarchy of invariant-subspace reduction and its staggered-unitary realization. Successive local deforma- tions reduce the invariant structure from IS fragmentation to the embedded spin-1/2 space Wemb and finally to a single scar tower. Local embedded dynamics couples states with different frozen IS labels and reorganizes them into representation sub- spaces. The staggered transformation relates the restricted embedded dynamics and the selected towers in the two realizations; full-Hilbert-space unitary equivalence is not assumed.

FIG. 2. Schematic illustration of the rigidity of the invariant-subspace reduction. A fully symmetric tower can remain invariant after Wemb is broken, whereas preserving a nonmaximal-spin, nonsinglet su(2) tower under the stated local constraints restores the entire embedded spin-1/2 space.
